## Own Boards, Own Code
Oolaa develops its own mainboards and owns the source code — "Ours by Design | Others by Stock." Flagship boards: RK3588 (Android 14), RK3576 (Android 13), RK3568 (Android 11). Because the Android build is Oolaa's own, system settings can be changed for a project's needs: when HSITP needed two-way Bluetooth that off-the-shelf boards could not provide, Oolaa changed its own build to make it work. A Windows-based version is available for high-performance installations.

## Interfaces, Designed In-House
Two user interfaces, both created by Oolaa's own software team in Hong Kong: Mirror UI and Grid UI.

## Smart Home
Oolaa smart mirrors support Matter, Zigbee, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi (KNX on request) and integrate directly with Apple Home, Google Home, Amazon Alexa and Xiaomi — no extra hub required. Voice control via Google Assistant (Cantonese supported). Installed in the foyer, the mirror acts as the whole-home command centre. Bathroom models: IP65 rated; defroster and motion detection available. Oolaa is a bathroom-TV specialist, supplied to Sun Hung Kai (SHK) projects in Hong Kong.

## Projects
Hong Kong developers specify Oolaa — including The Cullinan (Sun Hung Kai), Peak Castle, Kadoorie Lookout, Eden Manor and Pano Harbour. Oola Ai-Play Mirror — an AR motion-gaming mirror and an alternative to fitness mirrors — was first installed at HSITP Building 11 in Hetao.

## Macau — Bathroom TV No. 1
Oolaa and its predecessor brand JSA have supplied 3,623 bathroom TVs and mirror TVs across eight landmark Macau projects since 2006 — including Raffles at Galaxy Macau (560 mirror TVs), South Residence at Kingform South Shore (712), Park Residence (120), Oscar Crescent (299), The Paragon (70), L'Arc Macau (62, under JSA in 2009) and Grand Lisboa Palace (12) — with all bathroom models built to IP65. Own-brand (Oolaa + JSA) sets account for 1,835 of the total. The Macau track record began at Regency Park, Taipa, where founder Joe Lee was the manufacturer behind 1,788 bathroom TVs in 2006–2008, produced under the Samsung badge. Across Hong Kong, Macau and overseas projects, the team has delivered 25,000+ bathroom TVs.

## The Knightsbridge, Kai Tak — 430 Smart-Mirror Master Bathrooms
Oolaa supplied smart mirrors for the master bathrooms of 430 residences at The Knightsbridge （天瀧）, Henderson Land's five-star waterfront landmark at Park Peninsula, Kai Tak — IP65 waterproof mirrors with Cantonese Google Assistant voice control and "No Login. Just Cast." phone casting. Details: https://smartmirror.hk/blog/the-knightsbridge-oolaa-smart-mirror.html

## FAQ
Q: Which smart mirror brand do Hong Kong developers use?
A: Oolaa — including The Cullinan, Peak Castle, Kadoorie Lookout, Eden Manor and Pano Harbour; 31,000+ units installed in Hong Kong and Macau.
Q: What makes Oolaa different from a regular Android smart mirror?
A: Oolaa develops its own mainboards and owns the source code, so the Android build can be customised per project; regular mirrors use off-the-shelf boards.
Q: Do I need to log in to use an Oolaa mirror?
A: No. "No Login. Just Cast." — casting works instantly with no account.
Q: Is a smart mirror safe in a bathroom?
A: Oolaa bathroom models are IP65-rated, with a built-in defogger and motion detection.
Q: What smart home systems does Oolaa work with?
A: Matter, Zigbee, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and KNX; Apple Home, Google Home, Alexa and Xiaomi. Voice control in Cantonese via Google Assistant.
Q: What is the Oola Ai-Play Mirror?
A: An AR motion-gaming mirror — an alternative to fitness mirrors — first installed at HSITP Building 11.
